clue.text: Sailor found outside is ignored

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping round it, so one piece encloses another here

blocks.note: OS is short for ordinary seaman
to find something is to trace it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman returns from a voyage and finds the crew paying him no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' means traced, not established; OS (ordinary seaman) is a less familiar sailor than AB or TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise someone is to shut them out socially, so an ostracised person is pointedly ignored.

clue.text: Outgoing types required to co-operate with this

definitions.text: Outgoing types required to co-operate with this

blocks.note: surface reading: sociable, extrovert people
setter's reading: people leaving a polling station, asked to say how they voted in a survey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' looks like a word for gregarious personalities, but it means literally going out, of the polling station.
explanation.definitionFit: This survey questions voters as they leave after casting their ballots, to forecast an election result.

clue.text: Out in front – went first

blocks.note: the bow is the front of a ship
to lead is to go first

explanation.surface: A runner who led from the start was out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out 'bowled' when the ball hits the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowled is one of the ways a cricket batsman can be dismissed, i.e. given out.

clue.text: Children cycling make dangerous movement on road

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the final letter is carried round to the front

blocks.note: kids are children

explanation.surface: Children on bicycles swerving dangerously in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that skids slides out of control on the road surface, a hazardous motion.

clue.text: Players and politician known for 18, not 16? Reset possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many

blocks.note: Donald Trump, a politician known for idiocies (18) rather than self-deprecation (16)
the letters of reset rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe at a famous politician, defined by foolishness rather than modesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to 18-down IDIOCIES and 16-across SELF-DEPRECATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpeters are musicians, and players is a general word for people who perform on instruments.

clue.text: Saving money, make a meal

indicators.note: saving here means keeping something safe inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to make is to create
M is the abbreviation for money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Economising by cooking something at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon meal of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon repast, so it counts as a meal.

clue.text: Get a turn in carriage

blocks.note: to land something is to get it, as in landing a job
taken as written
a U-turn

explanation.surface: Taking a turn for a ride in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding top, a type of carriage.

clue.text: He hammered Spike not going the distance

indicators.note: failing to go the distance means stopping short, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: a thorn is a spike on a plant

explanation.surface: A boxer called Spike was knocked out before the final round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjolnir, so he is one who hammered.

clue.text: IT professional?

blocks.note: surface reading: a specialist in information technology
setter's reading: 'it' is a euphemism for sex, so this is someone whose profession is that

explanation.walkthrough: Capital letters make IT look like computing; 'it' as slang for intercourse is the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostitute earns a living from sex, the euphemistic 'it', making them a professional in it.

clue.text: Fish that's been smoked

blocks.note: first meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family
second meaning: the butt of a cannabis joint

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests smoked fish such as kippers; the second sense is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common river fish and, in slang, the stub left after a joint is finished.

clue.text: Worried Rishi's first PM with Department for Sleaze? At last!

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the name
one thing for another means swapping it in, as a replacement
at last points to the final letter of the preceding word only

blocks.note: the initial of Rishi
Clement Attlee, UK Prime Minister 1945-51
D is the abbreviation for department
the final letter of sleaze, which D replaces

explanation.surface: A jibe that Rishi Sunak was rattled by sleaze, like a scandal-ridden Whitehall department.
explanation.walkthrough: D takes the place of the last E of ATTLEE, which follows R: RATTLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rattled is nervous or unsettled, the same state as worried.

clue.text: Snake's horrible – Ruby recoils

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: mean in the sense of nasty
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A nasty snake makes Ruby shrink back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake is a verb here: a river that meanders winds and snakes along its course.

clue.text: Churchmen finally used Circle Line

indicators.note: finally picks out only the closing letter of the next word

blocks.note: CH is short for church and OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
the final letter of used

explanation.surface: Clergy took the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchmen' splits into Church and men; the Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here it is a line across a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a chord is a straight line joining two points on a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Amazed darn American rejected business

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so these letters go backwards

blocks.note: to darn is to sew up a hole
A is short for American
truck means dealings, as in 'have no truck with'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder from someone whose American business deal fell through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' looks like a mild oath; it is the sewing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, so it is a synonym of amazed.

clue.text: Manspreads when travelling (and more than once)

definitions.note: the symbol & stands for 'and'; the plural covers 'more than once'

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Men sprawling over seats on public transport, a recurring irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Each ampersand is the & symbol, a written sign for the word and, so several of them write it more than once.

clue.text: Charity of sorts protecting jobs

indicators.note: protecting means shielding something on all sides, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: kinds are sorts
lines of work are jobs

explanation.surface: A charity of some kind that safeguards employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in its older sense is benevolent goodwill towards others, which is kindliness.

clue.text: Deflect praise working on this quality

indicators.note: working means being processed, so the letters are worked into new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to practise modesty by brushing off compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: deflecting praise is exactly what this quality does.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-deprecation is belittling oneself, the modest trait shown by brushing aside compliments.

clue.text: Damnably difficult at first – landlady gutted by what might be said in court

indicators.note: at first picks out just the opening letter of the preceding word
a gutted thing has its insides removed, leaving only its outer shell

blocks.clueFragment: what might be said in court
blocks.note: deuce is the call of a tied score in tennis, played on a court
the opening letter of difficult
landlady with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A court case about a landlady who was cleaned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law; it is a tennis court. 'By' places the call next to the other letters, ahead of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Deucedly is an old-fashioned intensifier meaning extremely or confoundedly, the same mild oath as damnably.

clue.text: I see unfinished one's been accepted – they're very silly

definitions.note: a clause describing the plural noun

indicators.note: an unfinished word is missing its final letter
something accepted is taken in, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
a bishop's see is his diocese
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fool has been admitted somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb; it is a bishop's see, his diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocies are foolish acts or remarks, so they are things that are very silly.

clue.text: Lawyer's one question to flower girl – drinks?

blocks.note: DA is a district attorney
I is the Roman numeral for one
QU is short for question
Iris is a girl's name that is also a flower

explanation.surface: A lawyer cross-examining a bridesmaid at a wedding about the cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' looks like a bridesmaid; it is a girl's name that is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Daiquiris are rum cocktails with lime and sugar, so they are drinks.

clue.text: One is waiting with Madame in the same place

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to bide is to wait
M is short for Madame

explanation.surface: Someone waiting with a French lady, staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin used in footnotes to mean the same source as before, literally in the same place.

clue.text: Skinhead's determination to drink copiously

blocks.note: the head, or first letter, of skin
will is determination

explanation.surface: A skinhead set on heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' splits into Skin and head.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to gulp down drink greedily and in large amounts.

clue.text: Dirty dog's into special lady – no boy!

indicators.note: no means without, so the following word is taken away
going into means being placed inside other letters

blocks.note: S is short for special
a mutt is a mongrel dog
taken as written
a lad is a boy, removed from lady

explanation.surface: A dog getting into the company of a lady, with no boy around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No boy' works on lady itself: the boy is taken away and only the last letter remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty means indecent or obscene, the same sense as dirty applied to jokes.

clue.text: Unlikely a rich crossword setter's included - that's fantasy

indicators.note: something unlikely is improbable or odd, so the letters are put in an odd order
included means taken inside, so this piece goes within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter daydreams that one day crossword compilers will be well paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or wild fancy, so it is a fantasy.

clue.text: Talking plant? Give over!

indicators.note: talking means the word is spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: to seed ground is to plant it

explanation.surface: An exasperated reply to someone claiming plants can speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give over!' looks like the British exclamation meaning 'stop it!', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or rights is to hand them over to another, i.e. give them over.

clue.text: Against opening course originally? Only a bit

blocks.note: soup traditionally served as the first course of a meal
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Objecting to soup as a starter, and taking only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Soup is the course that traditionally opens a meal; the French loan word keeps its cedilla, dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a very small amount, a trace or hint, so only a bit.

clue.text: Close call with nothing to lose

indicators.note: to lose something means it is dropped, so a letter goes

blocks.note: a call is a shout
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A near miss where there was nothing at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close call' reads as a near miss, but Close is the definition and call the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a door or box is to close it.

clue.text: Stay over with dirty lecturer

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: L is short for lecturer
lewd means smutty, dirty

explanation.surface: Someone spending the night with a sleazy academic.
explanation.walkthrough: L and LEWD together, read backwards, give DWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or remain there, so to stay.

clue.text: Intrepid Duke lacking army, you claimed?

indicators.note: a claim is something stated aloud, so the sound of the word is what counts

blocks.note: D is short for duke
without ants, which march in armies

explanation.surface: A brave duke who went into battle without troops.
explanation.walkthrough: D plus ANTLESS, said aloud, sounds like the answer in an accent where aunt rhymes with ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dauntless means fearless and undaunted, the same as intrepid.
